caption:
"...and do not display yourselves as [was] the display of the former times of ignorance..."

Surah Al-Ahzaab (33:33) - context matters here: this ayah's direct address ('O people of the Prophet's household') is to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ specifically. Swipe through Arabic, English, Mandarin, Korean, Japanese and Malay, with that context noted on the citation slide.

Sources on the final slide.

sourcing.primary_text: Qur'an, Surah Al-Ahzaab (33), Ayah 33 - the 'tabarruj' verse, commonly cited in discussions of women's dress and modesty. IMPORTANT CONTEXT, disclosed transparently rather than glossed over: the ayah's own grammar directly addresses the wives of the Prophet (Muhammad's household) - the Arabic uses second-person feminine plural forms ('قَرْنَ', 'بُيُوتِكُنَّ', 'تَبَرَّجْنَ') and the ayah explicitly names 'أَهْلَ ٱلْبَيْتِ' (the people of the household) as its addressee. This ayah is one verse within a passage (33:28-34) that scholars widely read as speaking specifically to the Prophet's wives, though many scholars also hold that guidance addressed to them carries broader instructive weight for believing women generally by analogy. Per this channel's rule of never presenting primary text as a general ruling it does not itself state, the caption and citation slide note the direct addressee rather than presenting this ayah as a blanket rule for all Muslim women.
